title: Midjourney Pricing 2026 | Plan Comparison Tool
description: Compare all four Midjourney subscription plans—Basic to Mega—with 2026 pricing, fast GPU hours, relax mode access, and stealth mode. Find the right plan for your workflow.
intro: Midjourney offers four subscription tiers in 2026, ranging from $10/month (Basic) to $120/month (Mega). The key difference between plans is how many **fast GPU hours** you get per month—fast mode queues your job immediately, while **relax mode** (Standard and above) lets you generate unlimited images at slower queue times (1–10 minutes). Stealth mode, which keeps your images private and out of the public gallery, is exclusive to Pro and Mega. This calculator shows you exactly what each plan costs and what you get, so you can choose without second-guessing.

explanation:
## How Midjourney Plans Work

Midjourney charges by **subscription tier**, not per image. The core resource you're buying is **fast GPU time**—measured in hours—which determines how quickly your image generation jobs are queued and processed.

## How It Is Calculated

Each plan maps to a fixed set of resources:

| Plan | Monthly Price | Fast GPU Hours | Relax Mode | Stealth Mode |
|------|-------------|---------------|------------|-------------|
| Basic | $10 | ~3.3 h (≈200 images) | No | No |
| Standard | $30 | 15 h | Yes (unlimited) | No |
| Pro | $60 | 30 h | Yes (unlimited) | Yes |
| Mega | $120 | 60 h | Yes | Yes |

**Fast mode** submits your job to the priority queue — typical wait is under a minute. **Relax mode** (Standard+) uses a shared queue with 1–10 minute wait times but costs zero fast hours.

## Extra GPU Hours

On any plan you can buy additional fast GPU time at **$4/hour**. This is useful if you occasionally spike on a project without upgrading your base plan.

## Annual Discount

All four plans offer a **20% discount** on annual billing. That brings Basic to $8/mo, Standard to $24/mo, Pro to $48/mo, and Mega to $96/mo when paid upfront for the year.

## Commercial Use Rights

All paid plans include commercial use rights for the images you generate. The exception: companies with **more than $1,000,000 in gross annual revenue** must be on a Pro or Mega plan to retain commercial rights. Stealth mode (Pro+) is required if you don't want your brand assets appearing in Midjourney's public community gallery before launch.

## Stealth Mode

Midjourney is built around a shared community feed. On Basic and Standard, every image you generate is publicly visible. On Pro and Mega, Stealth Mode keeps generations private—important for client work, unreleased products, or proprietary visual assets.

faq.q: What does Midjourney Basic actually include for $10/month?
faq.a: Basic gives you approximately 3.3 fast GPU hours per month, which translates to roughly 200 images at standard quality settings. There is no relax mode fallback—once your fast hours are exhausted, you must buy extra time at $4/hour or wait until the next billing cycle.

faq.q: What is the difference between fast mode and relax mode?
faq.a: Fast mode queues your generation at the front of Midjourney's GPU pool—typical wait is under a minute. Relax mode (available on Standard, Pro, and Mega) uses a shared slower queue with 1–10 minute wait times, but does not consume any of your fast GPU hour allowance. For casual use, relax mode is often sufficient.

faq.q: Is the Standard plan ($30/month) enough for a freelance designer?
faq.a: For most freelancers, yes. 15 fast GPU hours produces roughly 900 images in fast mode. Combined with unlimited relax mode for exploratory work, Standard covers typical client project volumes. If you regularly need images to stay private before delivery, you would need Pro ($60) for stealth mode.

Only Pro ($60/month) and Mega ($120/month). Stealth mode keeps your generated images out of Midjourney's public community gallery—essential for client work, unreleased brand assets, or confidential projects.

faq.q: Do all Midjourney plans include commercial rights?
faq.a: Yes—all four paid plans (Basic, Standard, Pro, Mega) include commercial use rights for individual creators and most businesses. However, companies with over $1,000,000 in gross annual revenue are required to be on Pro or Mega to retain commercial license rights.

faq.q: How much does Midjourney cost per year if I pay annually?
faq.a: Annual billing gives a 20% discount across all plans. Basic becomes $96/year ($8/mo), Standard $288/year ($24/mo), Pro $576/year ($48/mo), and Mega $1,152/year ($96/mo). You pay the full year upfront.

faq.q: Can I buy extra fast GPU hours without upgrading my plan?
faq.a: Yes. Midjourney charges $4 per additional fast GPU hour on any plan. This is useful for project spikes—for example, if you're on Standard and exhaust your 15 hours mid-month on a large client batch, you can buy 5 extra hours for $20 rather than upgrading to Pro.

faq.q: When should I upgrade from Standard to Pro?
faq.a: Upgrade to Pro ($60/month) when: (1) you consistently burn through 15 fast GPU hours before month end, (2) you need stealth mode to keep client or unreleased work private, or (3) your business earns over $1M/year (commercial license requirement). If your main issue is just volume and queue speed, buying extra GPU hours at $4/hour is often cheaper than upgrading.

faq.q: Is there a free tier or free trial in 2026?
faq.a: No. Midjourney removed its free trial in late 2024 and has not reinstated it. You must subscribe to a paid plan to generate images. The entry point is Basic at $10/month (or $8/month on annual billing).

faq.q: How does Midjourney compare to Stable Diffusion in cost?
faq.a: Stable Diffusion is open-source and free to run locally on your own GPU. Cloud-based Stable Diffusion via APIs (e.g., Replicate) charges per image—typically $0.002–$0.01 per generation—which can be cheaper than Midjourney for very high volumes but requires more technical setup. Midjourney's advantage is a significantly more polished interface, consistent high quality, and no infrastructure management.
